questions.q: Why do automation scripts belong in a Git repository instead of on one person's laptop?
options: Git makes scripts run noticeably faster than running them locally
A script is code, and keeping only one personal copy means the team doesn't really have the automation if that laptop is unavailable
Laptops cannot execute Azure CLI or PowerShell commands
PowerShell scripts cannot be saved outside of Git at all
questions.explain: If the only copy lives on one laptop, the team's access to that automation depends entirely on that one machine staying available.

questions.q: In the cleanup-script pull request example, what did the code review catch?
options: An unused variable that had no effect on behavior
A syntax error that would have prevented the script from running at all
A missing safety filter that would have let the script delete resource groups based on a tag alone, without checking the name
A missing comment explaining what the script does
questions.explain: The reviewer noticed the loop trusted an env=test tag alone and asked for a -notlike "prod-*" filter before approving the merge.

Runs the script against a test environment automatically
Merges two unrelated branches together
Undoes a specific past commit by creating a new commit that reverses it
questions.explain: git revert reverses a specific commit without requiring you to manually reconstruct the previous working version.

questions.q: What does a saved-over script file (with no version control) lack compared to one in Git?
options: A history of previous versions to roll back to if a change breaks something
The ability to be run from the command line
Support for parameters like -Path or -Name
The ability to be opened in a text editor
questions.explain: Without version history, overwriting a script destroys the previous working version with no way to recover it.

questions.q: What does "team visibility" mean in the context of keeping automation scripts in a shared repository?
options: Scripts become publicly visible on the internet
The repository automatically emails the team every time a script runs
Anyone on the team can see what automation exists, read what it does, and check who last changed it
Every team member must approve every commit before it is saved
questions.explain: A shared repo means automation isn't scattered across individual laptops where nobody else can find or audit it.
